![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14192535/assets/1a7b132b3efcd909ec61421c956c6808cdbfd813123e2e9341fd0116d0d3deda.png)

What is the definition of the function $y=f(x)$ shown above?
question.worked_solution:
We will graph each branch separately.

- On the interval $(-\infty ,1],$ we have a line with slope $2$ and $y$-intercept $1.$ So the graph is the line $y=2x+1$ that ends at $(1,3),$ including this point.

- On the interval $(1,\infty )$, we have a line with a slope of $-2$ that passes through the point $(1,0).$ We can find the equation of this line using point-slope form:

$$
y-0=-2(x-1)\,⟹\,y=2-2x
$$

So the graph is the line $y=2-2x$ that starts at $(1,0),$ excluding this point.

Therefore, the function is defined as follows:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2x+1,\, & x\le 1 \\ 2-2x,\, & x>1\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: The graph is not a function
